title: Closures that capture
description:
Write functions that take and return closures:

```rust
fn make_counter(start: u32, step: u32) -> impl FnMut() -> u32          // each call returns the next value
fn compose<A, B, C>(f: impl Fn(A) -> B, g: impl Fn(B) -> C) -> impl Fn(A) -> C   // f first, then g
fn apply_n(f: impl Fn(i64) -> i64, n: usize, x: i64) -> i64            // f applied n times
fn memoize(f: impl Fn(u64) -> u64) -> impl FnMut(u64) -> u64           // calls f once per distinct argument
fn retry<T, E>(attempts: usize, mut action: impl FnMut() -> Result<T, E>) -> Result<T, E>   // first Ok, or the last Err
```

`retry` calls `action` up to `attempts` times (at least once, even if `attempts` is 0) and stops at the first `Ok`.
hints: A returned closure must own what it uses: declare `let mut next = start;` in the function and capture it with `move`, so each counter has its own `next`.
`memoize` returns an `FnMut` because it changes its captured `HashMap`; `cache.entry(x).or_insert_with(|| f(x))` calls `f` only for a new `x`.
